qt: to the Commission Paolo Inselvini (ECR), Carlo Fidanza (ECR) Subject:

Palestinian civilians in the West Bank are the target of escalating violence, intimidation and attacks at the hands of Israeli settlers. A particular flashpoint is Taybeh, a Christian majority village, where incidents of violence and intimidation have played out on land and property close to residential homes and places of worship. Cardinal Pierbattista Pizzaballa and other representatives of the Church have visited the community and called on the authorities to ensure its security. Serious incidents have also been reported in and around Qusra, where acts of settler aggression, property incursions and violence against Palestinian residents attest to the declining security situation and the danger of local communities being forced to abandon their homes. Civil protection, religious freedom and respect for fundamental rights are among the principles guiding EU external action under Article 21 of the Treaty on European Union. Can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What steps will it take to counter settler violence and protect civilians in the West Bank, including in Taybeh and Qusra?
What instruments will it use specifically to protect the Christian communities, their property and places of worship?
Does it intend to leverage EU-Israel relations to compel the Israeli authorities to take concrete action against the violence and ensure that local communities are able to stay?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.10.2026) The EU has long been clear about its strong opposition to Israel's settlement policy, which represents an obstacle to peace, and carries the risk of further instability in the West Bank. It remains the EU’s firm position that settlements are illegal under international law. During the European Council meeting on 19 March 20261, Member States unanimously condemned Israel’s unilateral actions to expand its presence in the West Bank and called on the Government of Israel to reverse these decisions, to abide by its obligations under international law and to protect the Palestinian population of the occupied territories. This is also reflected in the exclusion of settlement goods from preferential tariff treatment and the exclusion of Israeli entities in the occupied territories from EU programmes. The EU continues to strongly condemn the growing settler violence against Palestinian civilians, including violence against Christian communities, imposing sanctions on individuals and entities involved in violence against Palestinians in the West Bank and underlining the legal and reputational consequences for businesses participating in economic activities with Israeli settlements. The EU and its Member States are continuously engaging with the heads of Churches in Jerusalem. The EU has denounced hate crime incidents, property destruction and physical abuse and attempts to impose municipal taxation on Church and religious properties and the takeover of property2. Moreover, the EU reiterates3 its call for the upholding the Status Quo and protection of the special status and universal character of Jerusalem and its Old City.
